{{Short description|Research method}}
'''Behavior coding''', or behavioral coding, is a research method for evaluating [[Questionnaire construction|questionnaire design]] and survey interviewer performance and interaction.

Behavior coding has three main uses:<ref>{{Cite book |last=Dijkstra |first=Wil |title=Encyclopedia of Survey Research Methods |publisher=[[Sage Publishing]] |year=2008 |isbn=9781412918084 |editor-last=Lavrakas |editor-first=Paul |pages=54 |chapter=Behavior Coding |doi=10.4135/9781412963947}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Fowler |first=F. J. |title=Answering questions: Methodology for determining cognitive and communicative processes in survey research |last2=Cannell |first2=C.F. |date= |publisher=Jossey-Bass [[Wiley Publishing]] |year=1996 |editor-last=Schwarz |editor-first=N |editor-link=Norbert Schwarz |location=San Francisco, CA |chapter=Using behavioral coding to identify cognitive problems with survey questions |editor-last2=Sudman |editor-first2=S}}</ref>

# [[Pretesting (research)|Pretesting]] to assess respondent cognitive processing of survey questions
# Detection of problematic survey interviewer behaviors
# Interaction analysis to study how interviewer and respondent interact

Standardized codes are assigned to overt interviewer and/or respondent behaviors during the question and answer sequence in the survey interview, such as when the respondent asks for clarifications.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Kapousouz |first=Evgenia |title=The essential role of language in survey research |last2=Johnson |first2=Timothy |last3=Holbrook |first3=Allyson |publisher=RTI Press |year=2020 |isbn=978-1-934831-23-6 |editor-last=Sha |editor-first=Mandy |pages=23–46 |chapter=Seeking Clarifications for Problematic Questions: Effects of Interview Language and Respondent Acculturation (Chapter 2) |doi=10.3768/rtipress.bk.0023.2004 |editor-last2=Gabel |editor-first2=Tim |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pascale |first=Joanne |date=2016-06-01 |title=Behavior Coding Using Computer Assisted Audio Recording: Findings from a Pilot Test |url=https://www.surveypractice.org/article/2815-behavior-coding-using-computer-assisted-audio-recording-findings-from-a-pilot-test |journal=Survey Practice |language=en |volume=9 |issue=2 |doi=10.29115/SP-2016-0012}}</ref> The coding scheme is developed based on the research objective, but usually includes data collection-related variables such as question wording and interviewer styles.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ongena |first=Yfke |last2=Dijkstra |first2=Wil |date=2006 |title=Methods of Behavior Coding of Survey Interviews |url=https://www.scb.se/contentassets/ca21efb41fee47d293bbee5bf7be7fb3/methods-of-behavior-coding-of-survey-interviews.pdf |journal=[[Journal of Official Statistics]] |volume=22 |issue=3 |pages=419–451}}</ref> The coding is done using audio recordings of the interview, written transcripts of audio recordings, or via automated text analysis. Live interview coding is less practiced.<ref name=":0" />
